title: Content loading and full-text indexing
summary: Lessons go from files to the page through a build script, not a database: scripts/build-lessons.mjs validates content/ and writes an index plus one file per lesson for the frontend. There is no lessons table, no full-text index and no Ctrl+K search; this lesson shows what exists and what the planned index would take.

examples.title: contentcheck in small: collect every error, write nothing if there is one

annotations.note: The real script reads the ids from `content/curriculum.yaml`, and its allow-list has nine hosts (go.dev, pkg.go.dev, typescriptlang.org, developer.mozilla.org, react.dev, postgresql.org, nodejs.org, with www. variants). The H2 list is copied verbatim.

contentcheck scans every example file for LEARN markers, this one included. A literal marker naming a non-curriculum id here failed this very lesson's check while it was being written, hence the escape.

The frontmatter regex is the real one. The real parser is the `yaml` package, and validation against `lesson.schema.json` is a hand-written subset validator (about 80 lines) instead of ajv, as the script's comment explains.
The directory decides the id: `<track>/<module>/<NN-slug>` must be `track.module.slug`. `--filter` matches on the directory too, so a lesson with a broken id can still be selected and checked.
The real H2 check, verbatim: the headings present must appear in the fixed order, and the optional "How it works" may be missing.

The real marker regex: only id-shaped arguments count, so prose such as `LEARN(<lesson-id>)` in CLAUDE.md isn't a marker. On an unfiltered run the real script also scans `server/`, `src/` and `scripts/`.
Errors are collected, not thrown, so one run reports all of them. Any error means exit 1 and no file written: the frontend never imports a half-valid bundle.

examples.title: The generated module, the lookups, and the search that doesn't exist

annotations.note: The shape of `content/lessons.bundle.json` and of the private bundle verify-lessons reads: every lesson's frontmatter plus `dir` and `body`, and three maps keyed by path: example sources, expected outputs, fixtures. Until 2026-11-14 the frontend imported this whole object as one `.ts` module; it now gets the same data split per lesson.

A lookup by id, `Array.find` over every lesson, as the app's old `lessonById` did. `load.ts` now keeps the index in a Map by id, and its imports are typed by assertion (`index as LessonSummary[]`, `import.meta.glob<Lesson>`): no runtime check, it trusts the generator that validated the data.

The sidebar and lesson list come from `curriculum.yaml`; the content comes from the generated lesson data. `LessonPage` joins them by id, and a curriculum lesson with no content renders the "not authored yet" box.

The key schemes: `<dir>/<file>` for sources, `<dir>/<example id>` for expected output (a lesson's own file drops the `<dir>/`). Fixtures lose their `fixtures/` prefix on the way to the runner, so the program opens `seed.csv` in its working directory.

`toLowerCase` turns "İ" into "i" plus a combining dot, so "izolasyon" misses. `toLocaleLowerCase('tr')` fixes that and breaks the other side: "I" becomes "ı", so a query typed on a non-Turkish keyboard misses. A search has to fold İ, I, ı and i to one letter.
The proof: U+0069 U+0307, two code points for one visible letter. `.length` is 2, and a naive `startsWith` or highlight offset is off by one.

examples.title: The lessons table and search index the docs planned (not built)

annotations.note: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's ERD: a `search tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` column with a GIN index, so the vector is computed on write and every query is an index lookup. Weights mark title (A) above body (B).

Read what the stemmer did: "satırları" in the body became `satır`, but the title's "Satır" became `sa`. PostgreSQL's Turkish (Snowball) stemmer is aggressive and not always consistent; measure it on your vocabulary before relying on it.

`kilit` matched "kilitleri" in one title and "kilitler" in the other body, and the title match ranks higher. `websearch_to_tsquery` accepts what people type (quotes, or, -word) without raising syntax errors.

Lowercasing uses the database's own case mapping. This one (builtin C.UTF-8, see `scripts/setup-local-db.sql`) maps I to i, so "YALITIM" becomes `yalit` and misses the `yalıt` stored for "Yalıtım". The same trap as the JS filter, one layer down.
PostgreSQL 18 made generated columns VIRTUAL by default (computed on read), and those can't be indexed, which is why the ERD insists on STORED. The script stops here: an error ends a sql run.

use_cases: Content that should be reviewed like code: files in the repo, validated by a script, turned into a generated module
Small, read-only data sets a frontend can ship whole (docs, help text, a few hundred records) instead of serving through an API
Deciding between a client-side filter and server-side full-text search for a Ctrl+K box
strengths: No moving parts at runtime: lessons render with the backend down, and a broken lesson.md is caught by the build script, not by a user
Content diffs are ordinary text diffs, and every check (schema, ids, links, LEARN markers) runs before anything is written
`verify-lessons` builds a private bundle with `--out` and `--filter`, so several authors can check their own lessons without racing on the shared files
weaknesses: Each lesson is a separate chunk: opening one costs a request and a loading state, and a page that outlives a rebuild can ask for a chunk file that no longer exists (it shows an error and asks for a reload)
Nothing regenerates it automatically: not `npm start`, not `npm run build`'s prebuild. After editing content you run `node scripts/build-lessons.mjs` yourself

No search of any kind, and lesson ids join three places (curriculum.yaml, the generated lesson data, app-db rows) with no foreign key: renaming an id silently orphans its progress, notes and bookmarks
The import is typed with `as`, so a generator bug that changes the shape surfaces as an `undefined` deep in a component, not as an error at load

pitfalls.title: Expecting an edited lesson.md to show up
pitfalls.detail: The page reads the generated files. Run `node scripts/build-lessons.mjs` (Vite then hot-reloads), or `npm run gen:curriculum` after editing curriculum.yaml.

pitfalls.title: Renaming a lesson id
pitfalls.detail: Progress, notes, bookmarks, quiz answers and run history are keyed by the id as text. Treat ids as immutable, as the schema's description says.

pitfalls.title: Lowercasing Turkish with one function
pitfalls.detail: Neither `toLowerCase` nor `toLocaleLowerCase('tr')` makes İ, I, ı and i match each other, and neither does PostgreSQL's `lower` under a non-Turkish locale. Fold explicitly on both sides of the comparison.

quiz.q: When you open a lesson, where does its text come from?
options: Generated files bundled by Vite: an index in the main chunk, the lesson itself in a chunk of its own
The backend reads content/ on each request
quiz.why: There is no lessons route or table. `load.ts` imports `lessonIndex.generated.ts` for the header and loads `generated/<id>.json` with import() for the content.

quiz.q: You fix a typo in a lesson.md while `npm start` is running. What makes the page show it?
options: Nothing, the backend re-indexes content on change
Running `node scripts/build-lessons.mjs`; Vite then reloads the regenerated module
quiz.why: No watcher, SSE event or startup loader exists. The build script is the only writer of the generated files.

quiz.q: Why does the query IZOLASYON miss the title İzolasyon with both JavaScript lowercasings?
options: toLowerCase maps İ to i plus a combining dot, and the Turkish locale maps I to ı: neither gives plain i on both sides
quiz.why: The example prints both results and the two code points of the lowercased İ.

further_reading.title: PostgreSQL: Tables and indexes for text search

body:
## Concept

The curriculum's goal for this lesson is "files to lessons table to Ctrl+K". Two of those
three don't exist. What exists is shorter:

1. **Files.** `content/<track>/<module>/<NN-slug>/` holds `lesson.md` (YAML frontmatter
   plus prose), `examples/`, `expected/` and `fixtures/`. `content/curriculum.yaml` holds
   the full plan, including lessons nobody has written yet.
2. **Two generators, run by hand.** `npm run gen:curriculum` turns curriculum.yaml into
   `src/features/curriculum/curriculum.generated.ts` (sidebar, tracks, paths).
   `node scripts/build-lessons.mjs` validates every lesson and writes
   `content/lessons.bundle.json` (everything), `src/features/lessons/lessonIndex.generated.ts`
   (each lesson's title, header facts and unconfirmed claims) and
   `src/features/lessons/generated/<lesson id>.json` (one lesson's full content).
3. **A static import and a lazy one.** `src/features/lessons/load.ts` imports the index,
   which Vite bundles into the app. It lists the lesson files with `import.meta.glob`, so
   Vite emits each as its own chunk, and `LessonPage` loads one with `import()` when the
   lesson opens: the header renders from the index at once, the tabs when the chunk
   arrives.

The backend never sees lesson content. Its migrations
(`server/cmd/stacklab/migrations`) create `schema_info`, `runs`, `progress`, `notes`,
`bookmarks` and `quiz_answers`, each keyed by `lesson_id text` without a foreign key,
because there is no `lessons` table to reference. There is no `tsvector` column, no
search endpoint, and no Ctrl+K handler anywhere in `src/`.

## Coming from C/C++/Java/Python/JS

- **Static site generators** (Hugo, Jekyll, Sphinx, Docusaurus) are the closest model:
  Markdown in, a validated build artefact out, no database. StackLab's artefacts are a
  JavaScript module and one JSON file per lesson instead of HTML pages.
- **Java**: comparable to resources processed at build time into generated classes
  (annotation processors, protobuf). The generated file is checked in, like
  `curriculum.generated.ts`, so the app builds without running the generator first.
- **C/C++**: `xxd -i` or `#embed` (C23) turns a file into data in the binary; here the
  "binary" is the JS bundle. Go's `embed.FS` is the backend equivalent and is used for
  migrations, not content.
- **Python**: like loading a validated YAML file at import time, except the validation
  happens once at build time instead of on every start.

## How it works

`build-lessons.mjs` walks `content/`, and for each `lesson.md` it checks the frontmatter
against `lesson.schema.json`, the id against the directory, unique ids, that every
`prerequisites` and `compare_with` id exists, that example, fixture and expected files
exist, the H2 order, official-docs-only links, `nondeterminism_note` on `check: none`,
and LEARN markers. On success it writes the bundle and the frontend's files, each only
when its content changed, so an unchanged lesson doesn't reload open tabs; on any error
it writes nothing and exits 1.

Three flags exist for `npm run verify:lessons`, which never touches the shared files:
`--out <file>` writes only a private bundle, `--filter a,b` (with `--out`) restricts the
run to lessons whose directory matches, and `--allow-missing-expected` turns a missing
expected file into a warning while you generate it. verify-lessons then sends every
example to `POST /api/run` with `X-Stacklab-No-History` (or runs it in headless Edge for
ts-browser) and judges the output with the UI's own `judge.ts`, twice.

## Design notes

The docs describe a different design. ADR-0004 decided that "the backend loads and
indexes it into app-db at startup (upsert on content hash, delete removed lessons) so
search and the lessons table still work", with a `cmd/contentcheck` and a dev-mode file
watcher pushing an SSE `content-changed` event. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` draws the
`lessons` table with its `search` column. None of it was built: contentcheck is a Node
script, and what shipped is the alternative ADR-0004 rejected, "content in the frontend
bundle". The README's "it runs as part of the build" is also out of date: `prebuild`
runs `copy-wasm.mjs` and `build-lesson-libs.mjs` only.

For one user and a couple of hundred lessons, the shipped design is the boring, right
one: no loader to keep in sync, nothing to fail at startup, lessons readable with the
backend down. Its costs were a large main chunk, until the content was split per lesson
on 2026-11-14 (4.7 MB of first-chunk JavaScript before, 0.48 MB after), and no search.
If you add Ctrl+K, there are two honest options:

- **Client-side**, over the lesson index already in memory: titles and summaries are
  there (add tags to the index to search them too); fold Turkish casing as in example 2's pitfall, and it is instant with no
  backend change. This is where to start.
- **Server-side**, as drawn: a loader that upserts lessons by content hash at startup,
  the STORED tsvector with a GIN index, a search route. Worth it only if search must
  cover lesson bodies, which sit in per-lesson chunks the page doesn't load, or needs
  ranking and stemming.
  Example 3 shows what to check first: the `turkish` stemmer's quirks and the database's
  I/ı case mapping.

Either way, if lessons ever become rows, give `progress` and `notes` a foreign key with
`ON UPDATE CASCADE`, so an id rename stops orphaning learning state.
